claims.text: High-throughput molecular dynamics using machine-learning-calibrated semi-empirical potentials can accurately and efficiently determine melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The target HEAs are random solid solutions before melting.
The proposed simulations use semi-empirical potentials refined by machine-learning training on available experimental data.
Temperature-ramp simulations are run at constant pressure from below to above melting.
Atomic configurations and local chemical ordering captured during MD mediate the melting transformation.
The calibrated potentials accurately capture interatomic forces and phase-transition energetics.
Accurate interatomic forces and transition energetics allow MD to reproduce melting and yield melting points, fusion enthalpies, fusion entropies, and volume changes that mirror experiment.
Predicted melting temperatures, latent heats, and volume changes will agree with experiments within approximately 10–15%.
The approach will verify liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across HEAs.
Standard MD without machine-learning refinement or calibration often has larger discrepancies from experimental melting behavior and thermodynamic measurements.
The method is applicable to HEAs for which sufficient experimental training data exist.
The method may be less effective for compositions or behaviors outside the calibrated range.
Quantitative accuracy depends on the quality and representativeness of the training data and potential calibration.
Differential thermal analysis can provide experimental melting temperatures for validation.
Calorimetry can provide fusion enthalpy and entropy changes for comparison with simulations.
Density measurements or high-temperature X-ray diffraction can determine the volume change at melting.
Neutron scattering or other thermodynamic measurements can validate simulated liquid-phase structural properties.
The approach is falsified if errors consistently exceed approximately 10–15% across multiple HEA compositions or if simulations fail to reproduce the characteristic volume jump at melting.
